subject: Spectral3A p95 elevation — request for temporary SLA amendment & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@orchid.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: production latency spike - Spectral3A

Hi Jordan,

Quick note from our infra team — since ~08:40 PDT we've seen a step increase in p95 inference latency for the Spectral3A model serving our search endpoint. Our telemetry shows p95 sliding from 320ms to ~820ms across three availability zones. Throughput is stable. This started shortly after the June 9 model variant rollout (model-spectral3a-v9).

Attached is a short latency snapshot and a trace sample (orchid_latency_snapshot_20260609.log). We rely on the 300ms p95 in the contract for our checkout flow; this degradation is causing timeouts in a subset of customer sessions. We need Redwood's guidance on immediate mitigations and whether a temporary SLA grace window is possible while you investigate.

Short questions:
- Can you pin us to the previous variant (v8) while you debug v9?
- If pinning is possible, how long would a pin/traffic-fence take to enact?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Nguyen
Head of Platform, Orchid AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@orchid.ai>, Orchid AI Support <support@orchid.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Spectral3A p95 elevation — proposed short-term plan

Kimberly / team — looping you in. Orchid reports a clear p95 step after the v9 rollout. Can ops validate whether this is variant-specific (v9) or infra-related?

My proposal (short-term, action-oriented):
1) Pin Orchid traffic to spectral3a-v8 and enable prefix KV caching for that customer route. Expectation: immediate p95 restoration within 10–20 minutes once traffic changes propagate.
2) If pinning is not full-proof, activate a constrained traffic-fence (route-level concurrency cap) while we roll an emergency patch for v9.
3) Ask for a 36-hour temporary SLA amendment (p95 grace) for Orchid so they can continue running without automated remediation and to avoid churn while we investigate. I can draft the amendment form but need approval from Sales and Ops for credits/terms.

Attachments: none in this note; see Alex's snapshot.

Ben — can you confirm the commercial impact (credits / SLA language) so I can include numbers in the amendment form? Marissa — can you coordinate CS touches for any customers impacted?

Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@orchid.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spectral3A p95 elevation — proposed short-term plan

Agree with Jordan's approach. Quick notes from a commercial perspective:
- If we approve a 36-hour grace, standard practice is a token goodwill credit: typically 5–10% of that month's usage bill, prorated to the downtime window. We can escalate to a larger credit if downstream impact/penalties are documented.
- Any pinning that changes effective latency profile should be documented in the amendment (variant pinned, start/end times, fallbacks).

I suggest we keep credit language conservative for now and offer to revisit after postmortem. I'll prepare a draft amendment clause and attach it to the temporary_sla_amendment_form.docx.

Ben Carter
Sales Manager, Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@orchid.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spectral3A p95 elevation — proposed short-term plan

Thanks — ran an ops sweep and checked the rollout logs. Findings:
- The v9 rollout included a quantization kernel change for attention that interacts poorly with >1024 sequence windows in the current execution path on our older T4 pool. That explains why throughput appears normal but p95 spikes for longer sequences.
- Pinning Orchid's route to v8 is low-risk; we can enact a route-level pin in the control plane. Estimated time-to-effect: ~12 minutes (route update + warm cache).
- Recommendation:
  a) Proceed with immediate pin to spectral3a-v8 for Orchid traffic (I will perform).
  b) Enable prefix KV cache for Orchid's route to reduce cold-cache tail latency.
  c) Block rollout of v9 to remaining canary cohort until patch lands.
  d) Approve a 36-hour SLA amendment to cover the disruption window while we validate v9 patch.

I attached a short internal perf report (spectral3a_perf_report.pdf) and will post a mitigation runbook to INF-9123. After patching v9, we'll run a staged canary with tighter telemetry thresholds.

If Sales approves the credit language I can execute the technical changes immediately.

—Kimberly Park
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
